newsitem.title: CHINA: RESEARCH ALERT-Hutchison upgraded to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Hutchison upgraded to buy.

text.p: ING Barings said on Thursday it had upgraded its rating on Hutchison Whampoa Ltd to buy from sell and raised its earnings forecasts by 4.9 percent for 1997 and 3.6 percent for 1998.

"Over the past year, the stock has lagged the HSI (Hang Seng Index) due mainly to the lack of EPS (earnings per share) growth over FY97/98 on the back of the company's heavy reliance on large exceptionals for EPS growth, and going forward, large development profits," ING Barings said in a research report.
But analyst Nam Park said recurrent earnings are set to make a larger contribution to earnings going forward.

"We forecast core earnings to rise from 63 percent of total earnings in FY96 to 77 percent by FY99. We have identified the company's Hong Kong telecoms operations, Yantian terminal and Cheung Kong Infrastructure as the key drivers of recurrent earnings for FY97/99," he said in the report.
ING Barings forecasts 1997 net profit of HK$12.90 billion compared with HK$12.02 billion in 1996. For 1998, it predicted net profit of HK$13.68 billion.
ING Barings said Hutchison was likely to become the largest cellular operator in Hong Kong within the next 18 to 24 months.

"Hutchison Telecom is unique in Hong Kong as it boasts a rare advantage - a technological competitive edge. We expect its cdmaOne network to take the lion's share of mass market cellular telecoms growth."

ING Barings said the Yantian terminal was set to become Hutchison's premier port in southern China. "The recent rapid growth of throughput at Yantian provides tangible evidence of its potential to develop into a major port and earnings driver for Hutchison in the medium term."

It said Procter and Gamble-Hutchison, a manufacturing joint venture in China, was unlikely to contribute significantly to the group's earnings in the near term but would become one of the company's fastest growing operations.
"China earnings are also forecast to show strong growth over the next few years, driven by property development, manufacturing, and terminal and infrastructure operations," ING Barings added.
